subject: Pen test evidence: LOI, handback schedule, and redaction pathway
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@acme-payments.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request for full penetration test report + LOI question

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — helpful context for our payments integration. Our InfoSec team completed a risk intake and would like to review Redwood's most recent penetration test report and raw evidence artifacts (sample logs, POC screenshots) to complete our SIG/SOC2 assessment.

Two quick notes/questions from our side:
- We'll need a short Letter of Intent (LOI) or an NDA addendum that clarifies redaction allowance and evidence handback timelines.
- We generally accept redacted reports plus an embargoed access model for sensitive artifacts (time-limited S3 presigned URLs or an escrow transfer) rather than full unredacted copies.

Can you confirm what you can share, expected timelines, and whether Redwood supports temporary evidence escrow with described redaction controls? If easier, a short LOI template would help move this along.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Dunn
Security Ops Manager, Acme Payments
security@acme-payments.com

---
Attachments: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for full penetration test report + LOI question

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. High level: we can provide a redacted executive summary immediately and arrange time-limited access to sampled evidence under an LOI; full unredacted reports are only shared under stricter legal tooling (NDA with limited distribution + audited access).

Proposed next steps (suggested):
1) I circulate an LOI template that:
   - Confirms limited recipients (your InfoSec + legal),
   - Commits to returning or destroying evidence within 30 days of access,
   - Agrees redaction rules to remove customer PII and internal infra IDs.
2) We share a redacted exec summary (PDF) and a list of available artifact types (screenshots, exploit PoCs, sampled logs).
3) If you need more granular artifacts, we provision time-limited S3 presigned URLs and require (a) scanner/monitoring disabled for the session, (b) no rehosting of raw artifacts, and (c) acceptance of our evidence handback schedule.

Looping Legal (Laura) and Security (Karthik) to confirm redaction carve-outs and timeline feasibility.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request for full penetration test report + LOI question

Folks — reviewed Alex's ask. A few legal guardrails and proposed language: 

1) Redaction scope: remove any customer-identifying data, internal hostnames that reveal multi-tenant mapping, and API keys/secrets. We can allow sanitized PoC screenshots with all hostnames/hash-like IDs masked.
2) Evidence access: prefer time-limited secure storage (S3 presigned URLs) with access logging. Access granted to named individuals only; we require NDA/LOI that includes non-rehosting clause and a 30-day evidence return/destroy clause.
3) Escrow: We do not typically put raw reports in third-party escrow; if Acme wants escrow, we can accept encrypted handoff to an agreed custodian for a limited period but need explicit acceptance of risk allocation.
4) Operational timeline: redacted exec summary same business day after LOI acceptance; presigned artifact access within 2 business days after LOI + access approvals.

I'll attach a short LOI template and proposed redaction matrix. Marcus — please start with an exec summary share and the LOI draft. Karthik, please confirm if the evidence types below are safe to expose under our masking rules: sample logs (anonymized), PoC screenshots (masked), exploit scripts (we prefer to avoid raw exploit code).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
---
Attachment (to internal): LOI_Acme_Redaction_Terms.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request for full penetration test report + LOI question

Confirmed on our side. Technical clarifications: 
- Sampled logs: we will provide only event-level entries with IPs and customer IDs obfuscated (one-way hash) and timestamps rounded to the nearest minute to reduce re-identification.
- PoC screenshots: we will overlay or redact hostnames and any request/response bodies that include tokens or PII.
- Exploit artifacts: we will not provide raw exploit binaries or scripts. We can provide a high-level reproduction note that describes steps at a conceptual level.

Operational ask: when Acme requests artifact access, we will require an access request form that names the individuals and confirms acceptance of the non-rehosting and destruction clauses. We can automate the presigned URL expiration to 7 days for initial access; extend by exception.

Karthik
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for full penetration test report + LOI question

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a redacted executive summary (Acme_PT_ExecSummary_redacted_v1.pdf) and a short LOI that captures the redaction and evidence handback terms (LOI_Acme_Redaction_Terms.docx). Highlights:

- Exec summary: redacted for tenant identifiers and PII. Provides issue list, severity, remediation status, and timelines.
- LOI: names two Acme recipients (Alex Dunn, Jordan Park), requires acceptance of non-rehosting, return/destroy within 30 days, and requires signed confirmation before presigned artifact URLs are generated.
- Artifacts: if you sign the LOI, we'll provision 7-day presigned URLs for sampled artifacts (masked logs, screenshots); exploit scripts will be summarized only.
- Next step: please countersign the LOI and confirm the recipient list; once we have that I'll trigger artifact provisioning (ETA 2 business days).

If you prefer an encrypted-handback escrow to a third-party custodian, we can discuss but will need an explicit custodian and agreement on liability.

Thanks — Marcus
